title.en: Galle: three languages on a maritime inscription
title.zh: 加勒：海上交流中的三语碑铭

location.label: Galle, Sri Lanka; representative port location, not the present Colombo museum

summary.en: A stone inscription found at Galle preserves Chinese, Tamil and Persian texts connected with Zheng He’s voyages. Its inscribed date is 15 February 1409, while its transfer and installation in Sri Lanka belong to a voyage context whose precise dating is described differently in institutional summaries. The three texts record religious offerings rather than a uniform account addressed to one audience. The surviving object is now held at the Colombo National Museum. Because inscriptions can travel, the date on a stone need not identify when it was erected where it was later found. Maritime storage at Melaka forms a related but geographically separate history. The object’s text, movement and museum custody provide different kinds of historical evidence.
summary.zh: 在加勒发现的石碑保存了与郑和远航有关的中文、泰米尔文及波斯文。碑刻自署1409年2月15日，但运抵斯里兰卡及安置的具体编年，在机构概述中存在不同说法。三种文字记录宗教奉献，并非面向单一受众的同一篇叙述。实物现藏科伦坡国家博物馆。碑刻可以随人航行，因此石上日期未必就是它在后来发现地的安置日期。满剌加的海上仓储与此有关联，却属于另一个地理背景。碑文、移动过程及博物馆收藏分别提供不同类型的历史证据。

dateNote.en: 1409–1411 is a qualified inscription/installation context, not an exact erection date. Sources disagree over second- versus third-voyage placement. Galle is representative, while current object custody is in Colombo.
dateNote.zh: 1409—1411年是有保留的刻铭、安置背景范围，不是精确立碑日；来源对第二次或第三次航行的归属有异。加勒为代表点，现收藏地点在科伦坡。

sources.title: Trilingual Inscription (TribhashaSellipiya)
sources.evidenceNote: Inspected object register: Chinese, Persian and Tamil texts, inscribed date 15 February 1409, Sri Lankan provenance and present Colombo museum custody. Installation belongs to the early voyages; the modern shipyard-park wording is not adopted as a historical 1409 place name.

en: Chinese, Tamil and Persian texts record different religious offerings.
The inscribed date is 15 February 1409; the object is now held in Colombo.
zh: 中文、泰米尔文及波斯文分别记述不同宗教奉献。
碑刻自署1409年2月15日，实物现藏科伦坡。

title.en: Melaka: storage, monsoon timing and the Ming fleets
title.zh: 满剌加：仓储、季风与明代船队

location.label: Melaka; representative port center, not a surveyed depot footprint

summary.en: Accounts of the Ming fleets describe a storage and assembly base at Malacca, now Melaka. Goods and provisions could be held while ships gathered and waited for suitable winds. A museum account places this depot within the third-voyage narrative of 1409–1411; that framing does not identify a securely surveyed building site or a single foundation day. The port’s role depended on local rulers and maritime connections as well as visiting fleets. Warehousing, ship provisioning and attention to the monsoon help explain how repeated long-distance expeditions were organized. Their documentation connects practical maritime work with diplomacy and exchange. The Galle trilingual inscription is related evidence from the voyage world, but belongs to a separate Sri Lankan setting.
summary.zh: 明代船队的相关记述提到满剌加、即今马六甲的仓储与集结基地，货物和补给可在此存放，船只集结并等待适宜风向。博物馆概述把官厂放在1409—1411年第三次航行的叙述中，但这不能确定已测绘的建筑地点或单一奠基日。港口作用既与来访船队有关，也依赖当地统治者和海上联系。仓储、船舶补给及对季风的关注，有助于解释多次远航如何组织。有关记述把实际海上劳动与外交、交换联系起来。加勒三语碑也是这一航海世界的证据，但属于斯里兰卡的另一个地理背景。

dateNote.en: Focus 1409–1411 follows the third-voyage account; this is not independently verified continuous depot operation or an exact foundation date. The pin represents Melaka port.
dateNote.zh: 采用第三次航行记述中的1409—1411年作为关注范围，不表示已核实官厂在整个时段持续运作，也不是精确创建年；点位代表马六甲港。

en: Storage and assembly supported repeated voyages through the monsoon seas.
The museum account describes the depot within the third voyage, 1409–1411.
zh: 仓储与集结为季风海域中的多次远航提供支持。
博物馆记述将官厂置于1409—1411年第三次航行的背景。
